source.note: hand-written; a Claude Code session about a Node engines floor

units.text: CI is red on the node 18 job again. Can we just lower the engines floor to 18 so people on older LTS can install?

Before changing anything, a quick note on what the field does. The `engines` entry in package.json is advisory: npm prints a warning when the running Node is outside the range, pnpm refuses by default, and yarn ignores it unless `engine-strict` is set. Semver ranges apply, so `>=18` means 18 and anything newer, while `^18` would mean 18.x only. Lowering the floor is a one-line change, but it is a promise that the code runs there, so let me look at why the 18 job fails first.

Ran the suite under Node 18.20.4. 211 of 213 tests pass; the two failures are both in packages/core/src/ledger.test.ts and both throw `TypeError: crypto.hash is not a function`. `crypto.hash()` was added in Node 20.12 and 21.7, so this is not a flaky test, it is an API the project uses that 18 does not have. On Node 20.18 all 213 pass.
Hm. I don't want a polyfill or a createHash fallback branch, that's the kind of compatibility shim that rots. Let's keep the floor at 20 and make CI stop pretending we support 18.

Done. Removed the `18` entry from the test matrix in .github/workflows/ci.yml (it now runs 20 and 22), left `engines.node` at `>=20`, and added one line to README under Requirements: "Node 20 or newer (uses crypto.hash, added in 20.12)." The 20 and 22 jobs are green on the push.
Good. Also while you're in the README, can you make the install section use pnpm? We standardised on pnpm in January and the README still says npm install.

Updated: the install block now reads `pnpm install` and the scripts section references `pnpm test` and `pnpm build`. I left the npm-based one-liner in the Quick start since it uses `npx` to run the published CLI, which does not depend on the repo's package manager.

expected.content: The project requires Node 20 or newer because it uses crypto.hash, which Node 18 lacks; two ledger tests fail on 18 with 'crypto.hash is not a function'.
The user does not want polyfills or compatibility fallback branches to support older Node versions; they would rather raise the floor.
CI's test matrix runs Node 20 and 22; the Node 18 job was removed in February 2026.
The project standardised on pnpm in January 2026; the README install instructions use pnpm.
